answer: In PoA, every identity locks bonded collateral in an escrow, so correlated equivocation by k coordinated identities incurs a collective penalty proportional to O(k²), rather than k isolated fines. Once detected, asymmetric capital depreciation applies an exponential multiplier to the swarm’s loss, rapidly consuming its escrow and making fabricated diversity uneconomic. A raven cannot safely hide in a river of aliases, nor can cedar-backed capital evade correlated attribution.
